 Order
Dated this the 9th day of October, 2024 The 2nd respondent in the above M.A.C.A. is the review petitioner.

As per the judgment sought to be reviewed, the M.A.C.A. was allowed, holding that the appellant/Insurance Company is entitled to recover the compensation amount as per the award from the 2 nd respondent/owner/insured, in accordance with law.
The M.A.C.A. was allowed on the premise that the 2nd respondent herein was the owner of the vehicle at the relevant time.
Now, the petitioner/R2 would contend that, he was not the owner at the relevant time, and materials in support of the same has already been placed on record before the court.
Exhibit B1 produced before the trial court is the registration certificate of the vehicle involved, which would indicate that the 3 rd respondent in the appeal, one Mr.K.P.Aboobacker was the owner.

This fact is reiterated in Ext.A5 Final Report R.P.No. 645 of 2024 in M.A.C.A.No.1214 of 2008 ..3..
2024:KER:74862 preferred by the Investigating Officer in the crime registered in connection with the accident.

However, this matter was omitted to be brought to the notice of this Court at the time when the M.A.C.A. was heard, which caused the mistake in allowing the M.A.C.A. enabling recovery from the 2nd respondent.
On such premise, learned counsel for the petitioner seeks the judgment to be reviewed.

2. Learned counsel for the appellant in the M.A.C.A. (1 st respondent in the Review Petition) would submit that, the 3rd respondent was inadvertently deleted from the party array, as per a verified petition preferred by the counsel.

If in case, this Court is inclined to allow the Review Petition, then a fresh opportunity may be granted to the appellant to proceed against the 3rd respondent, who is now shown to be the owner by virtue of Exts.B1 and A5 before the trial Court.

3. This Court notice that, respondent no.3 is deleted from R.P.No. 645 of 2024 in M.A.C.A.No.1214 of 2008 ..4..
2024:KER:74862 the party array in the appeal at the risk of the appellant as per order dated 03.04.2019 in I.A.No.1/2019.
However, the same was based on a verified petition filed by the counsel.
4. It is clear from Exts.B1 and A5 that, the 2 nd respondent (review petitioner) was not the owner of the vehicle in question at the relevant time.
This aspect is also vouched by a reply obtained by the review petitioner under the Right to Information Act, which has been produced along with I.A.No.2/2024 in the Review Petition.
In such circumstances, this review is only to be allowed, as otherwise the 2 nd respondent (review petitioner) will be put to serious prejudice, inasmuch as the judgment directs recovery from him.
All the same, equities are to be balanced, so as to safeguard the rights of the appellant/Insurance Company as well, subject to the contentions to be put forward by the 3 rd respondent.
